teacher_moves: Imagine two identical balls leaving the same height. One is dropped and one is pushed sideways. Which lands first?
Look only at the up-down motion. What downward acceleration acts on each ball?
Vertical velocity changes +22, +12, +2, -8 m/s at one-second intervals. What do you notice?
Plot those values. What does the downward slope mean physically?
Say the relationship in words before we compress it into symbols.
learner_surface.worked_example: One second after launch, v_y = +12 m/s and a_y = -10 m/s^2. Find the launch vertical velocity. Explain the sign choice and perform a physical check.
learner_surface.independent_task: Two seconds after launch, v_y = +5 m/s and a_y = -9 m/s^2. Find u_y without model-revealing help and check the result physically.
